context:
Follow existing ClickHouse override patterns in other benchmarks. Check how
query overrides are loaded (likely a clickhouse_sql/ subdirectory convention).
The SQL change is straightforward: replace PERCENTILE_CONT(p) WITHIN GROUP
(ORDER BY col) with quantile(p)(col).
description:
h2odb Q9 fails on ClickHouse with SYNTAX_ERROR because it uses standard SQL
PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY fare_amount). ClickHouse doesn't
implement ordered-set aggregate syntax.

Fix: Add a ClickHouse-specific Q9 override using quantile(0.5)(fare_amount) and
quantile(0.9)(fare_amount). This is a 3-line SQL change.

Part of Pattern C (PERCENTILE_CONT rewrite) which also affects read_primitives.

anti_patterns.dont: modify base queries.py or default SQL files
anti_patterns.why: other platforms depend on standard SQL PERCENTILE_CONT

preserves.behavior: Base h2odb Q9 query unchanged - other platforms use standard PERCENTILE_CONT syntax
ClickHouse override returns identical column names and semantics as the base query

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/ -v -k 'h2odb and clickhouse'
verifications.description: ClickHouse h2odb override loads and uses quantile() syntax
verifications.expected: Tests pass confirming quantile() override for Q9
